exercise.name: Dumbbell Farmers Carry

reference.title: Dumbbell Farmers Carry
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Thighs, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (isometric grip, shoulder and trunk bracing while walking)

breathing.pattern: Brace and breathe behind the brace: short, steady breaths while you walk.
breathing.cadence: Steady steps, about 80-85 a minute here

prescription.load: User-chosen heavy dumbbells you can carry tall for the whole distance. Taylor & Reed 2020 suggest roughly 50-100% of body weight in total for rehab to general fitness, more for trained athletes.
prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbells, longer distance, or one-arm suitcase carries

cues.text: Stand tall between the dumbbells, pick them up with a hinge and stand up; arms long, shoulders set.
Walk with short, quick, controlled steps; stay tall and do not lean or sway.
Stop with the feet together, stay tall, then set the dumbbells down with a hinge.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning forward or to one side
mistakes.fix: Stay tall with the ribs stacked over the pelvis.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging or letting the shoulders droop

mistakes.fix: Hold them a little away from the thighs, arms long.

kinematics.peak: 55 cm steps (stride 110 cm), 110 cm per loop
kinematics.norm: Heavy farmers walk: shorter stride than normal walking (about 1.04 m vs 1.43 m) at a higher stride rate (Winwood 2014)
Steady, controlled pace (clinical opinion); heavy strongman carries used about 1.4 strides per second (Winwood 2014)
Upright, avoid side bending (Taylor & Reed 2020); heavy carries leaned about 12 degrees forward in strongman athletes (Winwood 2014)

kinematics.peak: Elbows ≈2°, dumbbells clear of the legs by 0.71 cm (rig shapes)
kinematics.norm: Arms long at the sides, shoulders set (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #291712, Dumbbell Farmers Carry, video (movement reference)
Winwood, Cronin, Brown & Keogh 2014, a biomechanical analysis of the farmers walk, and comparison with the deadlift and unloaded walk (Int J Sports Sci Coach 9(5):1127-1143)
Taylor & Reed 2020, increase hip and trunk stability with loaded carries for injury prevention, rehabilitation, and performance (NSCA Coach 7(3))
The quantification of muscle activation during the loaded carry movement pattern, 2024 (Int J Exerc Sci 17(1):480-490; PubMed 38665162)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
The dumbbell load is your choice: pick a weight you can move with the form shown for every rep.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Pick up and put down the dumbbells with a hip hinge and a flat back.
Clear the walking path; set the dumbbells down if the grip starts to slip.
modify: Grip-limited: lighter dumbbells or straps; shorter distance.
Low-back pain: lighter load, focus on staying tall.
regressions: Lighter dumbbells over a shorter distance.

muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the heavy handles the whole set; grip is usually what fails first.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the heavy handles the whole set; grip is usually what fails first.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders level and set, not shrugged to the ears or pulled down by the load.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders level and set, not shrugged to the ears or pulled down by the load.
muscleNotes.core: Carrying produced more trunk muscle activity than holding the same dumbbells still (Int J Exerc Sci 2024).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level on each single-leg stance.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level on each single-leg stance.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Drives each step and keeps the hips extended.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Drives each step and keeps the hips extended.
muscleNotes.quads_r: Support the bent stance knee under the load (the knee stays more bent than in normal walking, Winwood 2014).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Support the bent stance knee under the load (the knee stays more bent than in normal walking, Winwood 2014).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Push off at the end of each step.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Push off at the end of each step.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk tall (Int J Exerc Sci 2024: longissimus and multifidus more active while carrying).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk tall (Int J Exerc Sci 2024: longissimus and multifidus more active while carrying).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Keep the arms close to the sides.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Keep the arms close to the sides.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades set back.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the shoulder blades set back.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Swing each leg through under the load.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Swing each leg through under the load.
